1083
Nutritional Facts on Potassium
A potassium-rich diet is useful for cardiac patients who are try-
ing to lower their blood pressure using diet. If diuretics are also 
used, it is important to know if potassium is retained or depleted 
by the diuretic, and it should be monitored. Most patients with 
chronic kidney disease or on renal dialysis may need to restrict 
potassium in their diets. See Chapter 35. Because potassium is 
lost in sweat, athletes need to pay attention to the potassium in 
their diets. See Chapter 23.
There is no RDA for potassium. Dietary Reference Intake 
(DRI) is a general term for a set of reference values used to plan 
and assess nutrient intakes of healthy people. The DRIs for potas-
sium are stated as Adequate Intakes (AIs). For breastfed infants 
the AI is the mean intake; for older individuals the AI is believed 
to cover the needs of all individuals in the group, but there is a 
lack data to be more specific. AIs are given in the table.
